narrative: Material PL1__M6DD6978 exhibits intermittent, lumpy demand (CV=1.79) with only 42% of working days showing non-zero consumption and a detectable upward trend over the observation window. Lead times are moderately variable (CV=0.40) with a bimodal pattern suggesting two supplier delivery modes. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended: the reorder point of 360 units and safety stock of 238 units are calibrated to the 95% service level, while the order quantity of 629 units (above MOQ of 303) minimises total annual replenishment and holding costs. The current SAP policy of zero safety stock is structurally unable to achieve the service level target.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) continuous-review with EOQ-based order quantity
research_insights.selection_rationale: The (r,Q) model is appropriate for intermittent/lumpy demand because it triggers replenishment based on stock level rather than time, avoiding unnecessary orders on zero-demand days while ensuring sufficient buffer against sporadic large demands. EOQ balances ordering frequency against holding costs given the moderate annual demand.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity (3,502 units) is non-binding: safety_stock (238) + order_quantity (629) = 867 units, leaving 2,635 units of headroom. No capacity-driven reduction required.
